check1_cross_check.prior_source: D87 ORIN2 in-process interpolation via data_sources.device_recall_latency_s (the superseded source)
check1_cross_check.agree: under the 2x bar on the median

ONE question crosses the 2x bar and is EXPLAINED, not chosen between: the two quantities have different definitions. D87's is a TTFT indexed on FULL history tokens and clamps to 0.146 at <= 11k, while the measured one is a COMPLETION time on a near-constant ~5.5k-token RECENT prompt and does not scale with history length at all. The ratio spread tracks the proxy's token indexing, not measurement noise
agree, and the loader self-checks against it

check2_physical.rate: the measured 0.270 s delivers 2 output tokens on a 5,476 to 5,682-token prompt of which 5,392 tokens are CACHED, so about 110 to 290 tokens are actually prefilled. Implied end-to-end 5,524/0.270 = about 20,500 prompt-tok/s if the whole prompt were computed, and about 410 to 1,070 tok/s on the tokens actually computed
check2_physical.labelled: WARM PATH, explicitly. cached_tokens covers the RECENT frames on all 97 requests (cached_covers_frames_all true in the committed meta), so the 20,500 tok/s figure is a cache-hit artefact by construction and MUST NOT be compared to a cold prefill curve. The committed A6000 cold prefill is about 7,100 tok/s and the 4B saturated curve is 29,500 tok/s (costs.PREFILL_TOK_S); neither is the comparator for a warm number and no comparison is drawn
check2_physical.cold_counterpart: D155a: the COLD path on the same 97 is 3.354 s end to end of which 3.296 s is TTFT, and post-first-token time is 0.058 s cold against 0.059 s warm. The 2-token answer costs the same either way and the whole cold excess is a re-prefill charged before the first token. That is the physical component of Context Inertia on this workload, 12.4x, and it is consistent with a warm figure of 0.270 s
check2_physical.history_note: the 11k to 28k-token history is NOT the measured prompt: these are RECENT requests at 60 frames and about 5.5k tokens (r1_prompt_tokens, the full-history comparator, is 11,399 to 12,830). The 0.270 s is not a 28k-token prefill and is not reported as one

check3_distribution.near_constant: YES, and the INPUT is near-constant too
check3_distribution.input_is_near_constant_too: every part-1 RECENT request carries exactly 60 frames; prompt_tokens span only 5,476 to 5,682 (3.8 percent) and cached_tokens is 5,392 on all 97. A 22.4 percent latency spread on a 3.8 percent input spread is a DISTRIBUTION, not a constant, so this is expected rather than a caching or short-circuit artefact. The diagnostic the protocol warns about would be latencies identical to three decimals, and they are not
check3_distribution.artefact_spread_check: the by-deadline column is NOT a spread here: it is 0 flips, so there is no plausible spread to mistake for an effect
check3_distribution.averaged_out_check: the effect, if any, would be concentrated on the longest histories. Checked: the stratum does not exist under the measured source, because the measured latency does not depend on history length (RECENT prompt, near-constant). The slowest question, 0.3065 s, is still 10.2 percent of a 3 s deadline

check4_definitions.device_recall_latency: THIS RUN: measured WARM COMPLETION time (prefill + 2-token decode) on a 60-frame RECENT prompt, per question, Jetson AGX Orin, qwen3vl4b, vLLM. PRIOR COMMITTED: D87's ORIN2 in-process TTFT, two points (0.146 at 11k, 0.225 at 28k) linearly interpolated on FULL history tokens and clamped. SAME NAME, THREE DIFFERENCES: completion vs TTFT, measured vs interpolated, RECENT prompt vs full history. Reconciled by labelling: the old source stays reachable as LIVE2_DEVICE_LATENCY=trace and every output under it says superseded
check4_definitions.delivery: completion, D146 (1), on both sides of the comparison
check4_definitions.robot_deadline: 3.0 s on the _L3 family and 5.0 s on the un-suffixed family, read per question from the trace's own deadline_s and never from a literal. B3 moved the DEFAULT to 3.0 and kept the TRACE NAME ANCHOR at 5.0, so one name keeps one meaning
check4_definitions.device_only_row: the measured warm device answers alone, no cloud. Its CORRECTNESS is still D87's 4B-I x RECENT StudyO-Q4 set (A6000-produced); only the LATENCY is the Orin's. The row is labelled as that mixture and the mixture is not resolved here, because changing the correctness source is a methodological change

b3_trace_digest_proof.ruling: B3: ROBOT_DEADLINE_S default 5.0 -> 3.0 (D147), with the TRACE NAME ANCHOR held at 5.0
b3_trace_digest_proof.naming_decision: the _L<x> tag is appended when the deadline differs from the 5.0 ANCHOR, not from the default. Chosen deliberately: committed un-suffixed cells mean 5 s, so anchoring on the default would give one directory name two meanings. Consequence, stated: a run that now takes the 3 s DEFAULT is tagged _L3 exactly as an explicit --robot-deadline-s 3 run is, committed _L3 cells stay addressable under FROZEN_HEADLINE_SUFFIX=_L3, and committed un-suffixed cells stay addressable and stay 5 s

Both application sites are LIVE decision-timing sites in coordinator.py, which this session does not own, so adopting the measured value changes what the arm DOES and requires a RERUN, not a re-score. The one-line change the owning session needs: coordinator.py:63 DEVICE_ANSWER_CHARGE_S = DS.DEVICE_WAIT_MEASURED_S, or a per-question lookup keyed on the question id. Changing baselines/costs.py DEV_LAT_S instead would move committed dashcam, sim and map_bridge numbers and is a methodological change, not applied

answer_length_fact.consequence: P20's answer cap (512, unchanged per D155 (2)) is NOT the device's latency lever: a 2-token answer cannot be shortened. D155a measures the split directly: 0.058 s cold and 0.059 s warm after the first token, so 0.270 s warm is about 0.211 s of prefill-plus-fixed-overhead and 0.059 s of decode, and the 3.296 s cold TTFT is re-prefill of frames the device already holds. Where this bears on a conclusion: any device-side latency lever on this workload is a PREFILL or RESIDENCY lever, and the 12.4x cold-to-warm gap is the whole of it
